messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Sparrow (enterprise, Private VPC) — outbound error surge detected from private pool sparrow-prod-1. 5xx rate up, NLB target failing healthchecks in us-west-2. PagerDuty: page #1234. Runbook: <https://go/redwood/runbooks/privnet-egress>

oncall-ash: acked. grabbing initial logs, will triage. assigning priority P1. Affected: one Dedicated pool attached to Sparrow's VPC. ETA -> 5 min for first update.

sre-jamie: seeing repeated TLS handshake failures from NLB -> targets returning 504. healthcheck shows /hc timeout. Also seeing DNS NXDOMAIN spikes for egress-resolver.sparrow.internal.

eng-maya: jumping in. any config changes in last hour? release windows show no recent deploys to runtime. No infra changes in last 2 hours per deploy-bot.

network-oleg: quick note — security group rule for egress to 0.0.0.0/0 was recently tightened to allow only 443/80 from specific subnets. Could be SG block for managed NAT paths. checking.

support-ryan: customer (Sparrow) reported intermittent API errors at 11:42 PDT, high error rate from several services. Their telemetry shows increased retry/backoff and latency spikes.

oncall-ash: can someone run a quick curl from a host in sparrow-prod-1 AZ-a? I want to confirm path to external endpoints and healthcheck response.

eng-maya: from worker-az-a:
```
curl -v http://localhost:8080/hc
> HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
> upstr-error: upstream connection reset
```

sre-jamie: logs from runtime show connection attempts to our NAT gateway failing with ECONNREFUSED, then fallback attempts to egress-proxy which times out.

network-oleg: confirmed — the NAT instance in AZ-a is in a stuck state (iperf shows no outbound). Looks like conntrack table exhaustion on the NAT. We have a mitigation: spin up replacement NAT instance and shift route table. Starting now.

cust-success-lin: heads-up to Sparrow support: I'll message them that we're actively mitigating, expect partial routing to fallback for next 10-20m. No SLA breach expected if resolved quickly. :eyes:

oncall-ash: performing traffic shift to us-west-2-b fallback pool (read-only routing) to reduce customer errors. Running terraform apply for route table update.

ops-day-oncall: oncall handoff incoming in 20m. If this persists beyond the routing flip, escalate to infra-engineers for manual conntrack cleanup and consider autoscale for NAT.

eng-maya: terraform output:
```
module.route_table.aws_route.external: Modifying...
Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 0 changed, 1 destroyed.
```

sre-jamie: traffic shift confirmed. error rate dropped 63% within 2m. NLB healthchecks from AZ-a still flapping but overall customer errors trending down.

network-oleg: replacement NAT instance is healthy. I'm going to drain the stuck NAT then run `sudo conntrack -F` on it before decommission. scheduling drain now.

support-ryan: Sparrow replied: "seeing improvement, thank you". They asked for root cause and ETA for full recovery.

oncall-ash: short RCA: conntrack exhaustion on NAT instance in AZ-a causing outbound failures -> NLB targets returned 504s -> elevated 5xx. Mitigation path: spun replacement NAT, updated route table to fallback pool, drained and flushed conntrack on bad NAT. Work to do: tune conntrack, apply NAT autoscaling in private pools, add alert for conntrack usage.

cust-success-lin: I'll follow up with Sparrow with the RCA summary and timeline. Offer postmortem and recommended hardening (NAT autoscale + SG review).

eng-maya: open action items created: #INC-7894 (conntrack limits tune), #INFRA-4321 (NAT autoscale), #NET-2100 (SG egress rule review for tenant routes). I'll link PRs when ready.

oncall-ash: marking thread as "mitigated" but keeping it open for 60m for stability checks. If anyone sees re-escalation, ping here and page PG.

incident-bot: NOTE: customer impact -> partial (some endpoints experiencing errors). Incident state -> mitigated. Please attach logs to incident ticket: <https://go/redwood/incidents/4745009876>

ops-day-oncall: taking handoff. I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and run periodic checks on NLB target health and conntrack metrics.

sre-jamie: one more data point — conntrack peak at time of incident: 98% of table; thresholds were not alerting because default threshold was 100%. Raising alert threshold now to 85% and creating alert rule.

network-oleg: all NATs in the pool now show normal egress. SG change rollback not needed. I'll file a config audit to ensure no future traps.

support-ryan: closing loop with Sparrow: scheduled a postmortem call tomorrow 10:00 PDT. sending calendar invite.

oncall-ash: thanks team. great fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: This thread will auto-close after 60 minutes of inactivity."
